definition: Subcutaneous injection is a method of giving a treatment by injection instead of through separate intravenous doses. In this packet, it refers to a fixed-dose combined cancer treatment that was associated with less clinic time and lower healthcare system costs than intravenous administration.

reasons: The definition shifts the term from the administration route (“subcutaneous injection”) to a specific fixed-dose cancer regimen, which is not the requested sense of the term.

The packet supports a particular pertuzumab/trastuzumab subcutaneous formulation being compared with intravenous administration, but not the claim that the term itself refers to that combined treatment.
The comparative claims about less clinic time and lower healthcare-system costs are about the study’s findings for one intervention and are not appropriate as the definition of the term.

The definition states a general meaning of “subcutaneous injection” as “a method of giving a treatment by injection instead of through separate intravenous doses,” but the packet does not provide that general definitional wording; it only discusses a specific fixed-dose combination given as a subcutaneous injection versus separate intravenous doses for the studied drug.

The definition’s general contrast (“instead of through separate intravenous doses”) is only evidenced in the context of pertuzumab/trastuzumab in metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer patients, not as a general definition of the term itself.

The first sentence is therefore not fully supported by the packet’s content, even though the second sentence (fixed-dose combined cancer treatment; less clinic time; lower costs in the EsSalud context) is supported.
